description:
Which of these places is better for my dog: Carmel Beach or Asilomar, two parks, three hotels?
Sets two to six known places side by side, fact by fact.
Input: ids from search results ("carmel-beach", "asilomar-state-beach"); an exact name or a near miss resolves to the one clear match.
Returns one row per fact (dogs allowed, leash rule, where dogs may go, pet fee, weight limit, pets per room, restrictions) and one column per place, with confidence, freshness, who confirmed it, and a citation for each. An id that matches nothing is listed under missing with close matches while the rest are still compared (outcome partial); fewer than two found is no_match with suggestions.

ids.description: Two to six place ids from search results

response_format.description: 'markdown' for readable text, 'json' for structured data

name: dogpolicies_compare_places

accepted.description: With bad_input: each argument that could not be read, with the values it accepts

code.description: With an outcome other than ok: not_found, invalid, unavailable

did_you_mean.description: Close matches to what was asked for: towns, places, slugs or brands, best first

missing.description: Ids nothing matched, each with its close matches

nearest.description: When nothing is inside the radius: the nearest places in the data, with distance_miles

next.description: Calls that would answer the question, in words

outcome.description: Absent or ok: a normal answer. no_match: nothing in the data matches, see did_you_mean, nearest and next. bad_input: the arguments cannot be used as given, see next. partial: some of the ids were found, see missing. unavailable: a live source could not be read. None of these is an error.

answer.description: The one-line answer; while a seasonal rule applies today it leads with it (see today)

citation.description: Copy-ready citation: answer, source, date checked, record URL, license

closed_now.description: Present only when Caltrans reports this rest area fully closed now. Live feed data, not a verified rule: check quickmap.dot.ca.gov

fetched_at.description: When the conditions loop read the feed

until.description: Caltrans' end time (ISO); null when no end is set

confidence.description: stated: the place's own source says it; inferred_from_agency: an agency-wide rule; inherited_brand: the chain's policy, not confirmed by this hotel

freshness.description: fresh: inside its review interval; due: past it; stale: past twice it, confirm before you go; unreadable: the last check could not read the source

today.description: Only for a place with seasonal dog rules (plover nesting season, summer beach hours): which applies on the server's date, until when, and which starts next, with the source. Repeat sentence with the answer.

date.description: The date this was computed for: the server's date

rule.description: The seasonal rule in plain words

season.description: When it runs, in the source's dates: "July 1 to May 15"

in_season.description: true: a seasonal rule is in effect on that date; null: the source gives a season without dates

rule.description: The seasonal rule in plain words

season.description: When it runs, in the source's dates: "July 1 to May 15"

sentence.description: Leads answer and citation while a seasonal rule applies or starts within 14 days; null otherwise

rule.description: The seasonal rule in plain words

season.description: When it runs, in the source's dates: "July 1 to May 15"

undated.description: Seasons the source states without dates: not known to apply

rule.description: The seasonal rule in plain words

season.description: When it runs, in the source's dates: "July 1 to May 15"

uid.description: Stable id that survives a rename

resolved_from.description: Set when a word was read as the value the tool uses: hotel as lodging, NB as north. Each key is the argument; asked is what was sent, used what it was read as

title: Compare places side by side
